title: Grateful Dead Live at Harding Theatre on 1971-11-07

ai_review.summary: A high‑energy November 1971 Harding Theatre show captured on a FM‑matrix feed – fuzzy in spots but brimming with smoking renditions of Me & My Uncle, Dark Star/Other One and the classic NFA→Goin’ Down The Road Feeling Bad→NFA run.
ai_review.review: The performance is consistently described as one of the band’s finest of ’71, highlighted by a scorching Me and My Uncle, an epic Dark Star → The Other One suite and flawless transitions like Not Fade Away → Goin’ Down the Road Feeling Bad → Not Fade Away.  Technically the recording suffers from FM‑broadcast interference, occasional drop‑outs and a bit of keyboard distortion, but listeners deem it still very listenable and worth repeated spins.

ai_rating.rationale: Over ten detailed 5‑star reviews praise the musical performance with only minor, consistent comments about audio fuzziness; the weighted average of show (≈5) and recording (≈4) yields a high overall rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: FM broadcast feed introduces extra‑heterodynamic interference, occasional dropouts and slight keyboard distortion; overall clarity is acceptable but not pristine.

standout_songs: Not Fade Away > Goin' Down the Road Feeling Bad > Not Fade Away
show_quality.setlist_flow: The set is praised for seamless segues—especially the NFA→GDTRFB→NFA sequence and the Other One/Me & My Uncle/Other One sandwich—creating a flowing, high‑impact marathon that kept the audience enthralled.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His '57 Strat is described as guttural, solar‑plexus‑punching and he delivers a falsetto vocal on Comes a Time; overall guitar work is highlighted as smoking throughout.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for his banter and bass presence; no specific criticism of his playing.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith’s piano is mentioned positively despite occasional distortion; reviewers note this was early in his tenure but still strong.
